category_title: Elementary student with Duchenne muscular dystrophy exhibiting task-avoidant and attention-seeking disruptive behaviors
minimal_context: Philip is in his English language classroom and is asked to read his homework.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright class, it is time for our English language lesson. Please take out your notebooks so we can read your homework.

STUDENT: (Interrupts the lesson speaking out of turn) I am not reading that!

TUTOR: Philip, it is time to read. Please look at your assignment.

STUDENT: (Leaves his seat without permission and moves to another place in the classroom) No!

TUTOR: (Steps forward to drive him to his seat) Philip, you need to come back and sit in your chair right now.

STUDENT: (Runs around the classroom while singing) La la la! (Falls on the ground and cries as he attempts to escape from the teacher)

options.A: Have the student use a computer application to take notes, organize his English homework, and archive past reading assignments throughout the semester during class.
options.B: Ask the student to choose his own creative English projects based on his strengths and interests instead of reading the assigned homework during the lesson.
options.C: Alternate reading for a few minutes, writing in notebooks for a few minutes, talking as a class, and sharing with a partner during the English lesson.
options.D: Provide a smiley face sticker at the end of every 45-minute period if the student completes his English homework on his own or asks for help by raising his hand.
